newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel backs Novartis drug for RA.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel backs Novartis drug for RA.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Arthritis Advisory Committee on Tuesday recommended FDA approval of Novartis Pharmaceutical's oral microemulsion form of cyclosporin, Neoral, for treatment of severe active rheumatoid arthritis (RA).
But the panel said the drug should only be used in patients who had failed two of several other available RA drugs, and who have normal kidney function.
The panel added that Neoral should not be used in patients who have blood pressure readings greater than 140/90, citing the drug's tendency to cause hypertension.
The panel said it was concerned about safety, particularly the drug's potential to cause kidney disease.

Novartis said that renal dysfunction can be controlled if Neoral's doses are kept below four milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day, and recommended that patients' kidney function be monitored every two weeks for the first three months, and monthly thereafter.
The committee also said the drug can be used in combination with methotrexate, which Novartis was proposing.
Neoral is similar to Novartis' Sandimmune, which was approved in 1983, but is absorbed better, the company said.
Neoral was approved in the United States in 1995 to help prevent transplant rejection, and has been approved in 70 countries to treat RA.
SangStat Medical Corp in November filed for FDA approval of its generic version of cyclosporine, which would be a competitor to Neoral. Novartis has petitioned the FDA to block the approval.
Sergio Traversa, an analyst with Mehta & Isaly, said that if approved, SangStat's drug, even if it is lower priced, should not dramatically affect Novartis' sales.
The FDA does not have to follow the advisory panel's advice but usually does.
